review.summary: Phase 16 (Portkey access-policy implementation) meets its accepted-plan acceptance criteria with real, verifiable evidence. All five pinned operations exist as a standalone, explicitly key-authenticated control-plane client (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/gateway/access_policies.rs) with handwritten typed models, contract-derived request validation, a registered offline example, a five-operation ledger bound by the Node verifier, a 38-case fixture corpus independently validated against the pinned OpenAPI with ajv, and 8 new Rust contract tests. I checked the implementation field-by-field against contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/contract.json: routes, verb set, security scheme, name 1..64, nullable description max 256, subjects/targets minItems 1, version minimum 1, effect enum, the twelve list query parameters with maxLength 36/36/100/64/255 and minimum-0 integers, RFC3339 date-time, MCP tools required vs provider models optional, and the ALL-or-nonempty-list selector all match; the documented create effect inference (deny only when both user ANY and agent ANY are present, otherwise allow, and allow requires a specific subject) is implemented exactly as the pinned description states, and update omission is left to the server. Security posture reuses hardened core primitives: require_auth(AuthKind::Runtime) rejects None/Scan/OAuth at construction; writes use RawRequest::new (replay_safe=false, runtime_retries=None) so no mutation is replayed even with with_retries(5), while reads use RawRequest::read; path IDs go through the centralized UUID predicate plus encode_segment traversal rejection; endpoint admission and destination policy run in preflight; 409 surfaces as a plain HTTP conflict with no hidden GET or merge; bodies are bounded by serialize_bounded and re-decoded through json_decode (reserved-protocol-key fail-closed) before dispatch; extension maps cannot shadow typed fields; new option/model types have redacted Debug; no unsafe, no unwrap, no new dependencies, version still 0.2.0, no attachment to AIGatewayClient OAuth planes. Evidence is executed rather than claimed: docs/checks/phase-16.json records 9 commands (source_sha256 cf54f553..., source_unchanged true, all exit 0), including node tools/portkey-access.mjs --check (5 operations, 9 schemas, 38 independently checked fixtures), test_ci.py (31 tests), test_portkey_access.py (8), test_review_phase.py (30), and scripts/check-rust.py on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 for the gateway feature, whose child reports show fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test/examples/doc all green with the 8 new portkey tests passing. Remaining findings are non-blocking: the new product entry point lacks the repo-required constructor rustdoc and compiled no_run example, a local Debug-redaction macro duplicates the shared crate::redaction::redacted_debug!, the fixture corpus does not record or independently bind the reasons its sdkValid expectations diverge from schemaValid, invalid-UUID coverage exists only for get, the whitespace guard was not extended to the new untracked JSON artifacts, header assertions check absence instead of the exact set, and phase-status scope_evidence is duplicated and omits this phase's own check reports.

findings.description: AccessPoliciesClient is a new product entry point, but its constructor has no item documentation and no compiled example. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:79-92 states the current rustdoc coverage boundary: every product facade constructor (ManagementClient, DlpClient, IamScopesClient, ModelSecurityClient, RedTeamClient, AIGatewayClient, RuntimeClient, AgentGuardClient) must have item documentation plus a short compiled no_run example explaining its Cargo feature, credential plane and endpoint requirements, and that 'adding a product entry point requires the same item documentation and compiled example during review'. The doctest inventory in docs/checks/phase-16-rust-1.99.0-gateway.json:90 shows only three facade doctests (gateway/mod.rs:123, runtime.rs:33, iam/scopes.rs:33) and none for access policies; new(), client(), get() and delete() carry no rustdoc at all. The struct-level doc at lines 126-129 is good but is not the required constructor contract.
findings.required_fix: Add rustdoc on AccessPoliciesClient::new stating the gateway feature, the required Runtime key credential plane, the caller-selected/admitted control-plane origin, and the no-replay/409 behavior, with a compiled no_run example in the style of crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/gateway/runtime.rs:33; add short docs to client(), get() and delete(); and add AccessPoliciesClient to the entry-point list in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:79-88.

findings.description: The file defines a private macro_rules! redacted! that is byte-for-byte equivalent to the existing shared crate::redaction::redacted_debug! (crates/scm-sdk/src/redaction.rs:2-13, same concat!(stringify!($ty), "([REDACTED])") body and same multi-type repetition), which was introduced specifically to centralize option Debug redaction after the phase-5 review advisory (docs/phase-status.json:325). Duplicating it means a future change to the shared redaction policy will silently not apply to the ten access-policy types redacted at lines 231, 243, 280, 321, 334 and 388-399.
findings.required_fix: Delete the local macro at access_policy_models.rs:8-14 and use crate::redaction::redacted_debug!(...) for all the access-policy types instead.

findings.description: Cases whose SDK expectation deliberately diverges from OpenAPI validity carry no recorded reason and no independent binding to the upstream text that justifies them: 'one ANY inferred allow' (schemaValid true / sdkValid false, line 302), 'group ANY invalid' (line 322), 'explicit allow both ANY' (line 344), 'update explicit allow' (line 659), 'unknown response effect' (line 697) and 'unknown target' (line 706). tools/portkey-access.mjs:73-76 only asserts schemaValid with ajv, and crates/scm-sdk/tests/portkey_access_contracts.rs:427 only asserts sdkValid against the implementation, so the semantic rules the client enforces (plan lines 69-78) are pinned by a fixture flag written alongside the code rather than checked against the pinned description. I verified manually that every divergence matches contract.json:21 and 413 and the response open-vocabulary policy, so this is an evidence/drift-protection gap, not an incorrect rule.
findings.required_fix: Add a required 'reason' field to every fixture case where schemaValid != sdkValid, assert its presence in tools/portkey-access.mjs, and add a tools/test_portkey_access.py assertion that contract.json's create description contains the ANY/ANY deny-inference sentence and the allow-requires-a-specific-subject sentence that these cases encode.

findings.description: Invalid path-identifier rejection is only exercised for get(). update() validates the UUID inside its body-validation closure (access_policies.rs:298) and delete() validates it in a separate options.run block (access_policies.rs:333); neither path is covered, so a future reordering that dropped common::uuid from update or delete would pass the suite. The plan's phase-16 case list names 'invalid UUID' without restricting it to reads.
findings.required_fix: Extend the bad-identifier loop at lines 229-239 to also call client.update(id, &update(), None) and client.delete(id, None) and assert ErrorKind::Validation with no dispatch for each.

findings.description: The authored-file whitespace/newline guard added for the phase-15 review finding still lists only the phase-15 artifacts (plan, research, mjs, this test, source.json, contract.json). The phase-16 authored non-Rust artifacts contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/model-fixtures.json and operations.json are not included, and the two git diff --check commands in the phase-16 gate (docs/checks/phase-16.json:9-55) cannot see them because they are untracked. I confirmed by search that neither file currently has trailing whitespace, so this is a missing guard rather than a defect.
findings.required_fix: Add model-fixtures.json and operations.json (and the new Rust sources, which cargo fmt already covers) to the tuple at tools/test_portkey_access.py:69 so the newline/trailing-whitespace guard applies to this phase's own authored artifacts.

findings.description: The wire test asserts the sensitive x-portkey-api-key value and the absence of authorization, x-tsg-id and x-portkey-provider, but never asserts the exact header set, so additional headers could be attached silently. Every request also carries the SDK-wide service-name: api and PAN-AIRS user-agent defaults (crates/scm-sdk/src/engine.rs:24-32) to this third-party control-plane origin; that matches established behavior for the Portkey runtime client, which asserts the exact set ["service-name", "user-agent", "x-portkey-api-key"] at crates/scm-sdk/tests/representative_clients.rs:412, but the new client has no equivalent assertion.
findings.required_fix: Assert the exact sorted header-name set on all five new requests, in the style of crates/scm-sdk/tests/representative_clients.rs:412.

findings.description: The phase-16 scope_evidence list repeats four entries verbatim (source.json, contract.json, the plan and tools/portkey-access.mjs appear twice at lines 3361-3368), carries docs/checks/phase-15.json, and omits this phase's own executed evidence: docs/checks/phase-16.json, docs/checks/phase-16-rust-1.89.0-gateway.json and docs/checks/phase-16-rust-1.99.0-gateway.json. Phase 15 received the same class of bookkeeping finding (docs/phase-status.json:3316-3321).
findings.required_fix: Deduplicate the phase-16 scope_evidence list and add the three phase-16 check reports (phase-17's identical duplication at lines 3393-3400 should be cleaned up at the same time).

findings.description: Several new statements are single lines of 300-400+ characters (line 84, line 85, line 104 is literally 'let query:AccessPolicyListOptions=serde_json::from_value(json!({...}))' with no spaces around ':' or '='). rustfmt silently skips statements it cannot fit within max_width, which is why cargo fmt --check still passes (docs/checks/phase-16-rust-1.99.0-gateway.json:30); the result is that the new test file's layout is effectively unchecked and hard to review line-by-line. This continues the dense-layout pattern that earlier reviews already raised (docs/phase-status.json:325, 3346-3351).
findings.required_fix: Split the long literal bindings (lines 84-85 and 104) into multiple statements or pre-bound json! values so rustfmt formats them, then re-run the two check-rust.py gates.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-16.json:3-6 records source_sha256 cf54f553d3a66015f04b45e72621aedd57f66dd0a558199a40b2994b16cc6c1d, source_unchanged true and passed true; the 9 recorded commands exactly equal tools/check_phase.py:71-76 commands_for(16), and tools/review_phase.py:43-60 shows the fingerprint covers tracked and untracked non-ignored files, so the new untracked implementation files are inside the hashed source.

docs/checks/phase-16.json:69 shows node tools/portkey-access.mjs --check emitting the five expected operationIds with security [{"Portkey-Key":[]}], 9 schemas and {"independentlyCheckedFixtures":38}; tools/portkey-access.mjs:65-78 performs that fixture check with pinned ajv 8.20.0 / ajv-formats 3.0.1 (tools/package.json:9-10) against the extracted contract, and :79-93 binds every operation to a real pub async fn, operation-name literal and test function.

docs/checks/phase-16-rust-1.99.0-gateway.json:90 and the 1.89.0 sibling show all six cargo steps (fmt --check, check --all-targets, clippy -D warnings, test, test --examples, doc) at exit 0, with 'running 8 tests' for portkey_access_contracts and all eight new tests passing; the --examples run shows examples/access_policies.rs compiled only (0 tests), so the example is compile-verified rather than executed.

Contract conformance verified directly: contract.json:722-758 (name minLength 1/maxLength 64, nullable description maxLength 256, effect enum, subjects/targets minItems 1, enabled default true) against access_policies.rs:64-125 and access_policy_models.rs:118-152; contract.json:769-772 version minimum 1 against access_policies.rs:71-78; contract.json:209-283 query maxLengths 36/36/100/64/255, date-time and minimum-0 paging against access_policies.rs:219-238; contract.json:651-707 tools/models selectors against access_policies.rs:52-63 and :117-123.

The documented semantics in contract.json:21 ('allow policies must name at least one specific user, group, or agent'; omitted effect is 'deny if subjects contains both a user ANY and an agent ANY entry, otherwise allow') are implemented exactly at access_policies.rs:89-116, and contract.json:413 (update keeps stored name/description/effect/enabled) is honored by the Optional/Patch skip_serializing_if fields at access_policy_models.rs:159-168 plus the assertions at portkey_access_contracts.rs:284-292.

No-replay for mutations is structural, not incidental: engine.rs:49-67 gives RawRequest::new replay_safe=false and RawRequest::read replay_safe=true, engine.rs:1172-1236 only retries when replay_safe or runtime_retries is set, and portkey_access_contracts.rs:295-323 proves one dispatch for 409, 500 and a transport failure even with with_retries(5), with RemoteOutcome::Unknown preserved for the ambiguous case and no key in Debug/Display output.

Credential-plane and destination enforcement verified: engine.rs:489-513 require_auth(Runtime) accepts only Authentication::RuntimeKey, auth.rs:801-805 attaches only the sensitive x-portkey-api-key, engine.rs:908-922 enforces endpoint admission plus DestinationPurpose::Api policy, and portkey_access_contracts.rs:440-499 shows None/Scan/OAuth constructions rejected with ErrorKind::Configuration (the OAuth token provider panics if ever used) and an empty OriginPolicy producing ErrorKind::Destination with zero dispatches.

Bounded, fail-closed request handling: access_policies.rs:142-157 serializes with serialize_bounded(max_request_bytes) and re-decodes through crate::json_decode::from_slice (the phase-8 reserved-protocol-key hardening) inside options.run, so cancellation, deadline and request-limit errors all precede dispatch, as asserted at portkey_access_contracts.rs:346-377; response bounds and decode strictness are asserted at :324-343.

Extension-collision safety and faithful JSON: access_policies.rs:26-51 rejects any extension key that shadows a typed field (exercised at portkey_access_contracts.rs:216-222 with extra 'effect'), and portkey_access_contracts.rs:83-186 asserts the literal verb/path/host/header/body/query for all five calls, including exact ordered query pairs with zero paging, false enabled, Unicode and reserved characters, plus byte-identical response round-trips for unknown effect, unknown target variants and nested nulls.
limitations: Read-only review: I executed nothing. All pass/fail claims rest on the recorded reports (docs/checks/phase-16.json and the two check-rust.py child reports), whose source_sha256 matches the reviewed source and whose per-command stdout/stderr I inspected; I could not independently re-run cargo, node or ajv.

I did not inspect credential, tenant-registration or .local credential material, so the operations.json liveAcceptance 'not_attempted' reason (no compatible key/control-plane registration selected) is taken at face value; it is consistent with the plan's read-only live restriction and no live evidence is claimed anywhere.
ajv's handling of OpenAPI 3.0 'nullable' is inferred from the recorded passing run (the nullable-description cases are expected-valid and the check exits 0) rather than from executing ajv myself.
The example's main() body is compile-verified only; cargo test --examples does not run it, so its asserted offline behavior is unexecuted until the phase-17 packaged-consumer step.

I judged phase 16 only. Version bump, changelog/feature docs/README/NOTICE updates, frozen ledger and dependency re-runs, minimal/default/all feature matrices, CI wiring, archive proofs and publication are phase-17 deliverables and were not assessed; the 'planned' live status of these endpoints is likewise not a phase-16 gap.
I did not re-audit historical phases 1-15 infrastructure; prior accepted release evidence was treated as historical and not as acceptance for this new source.
